.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 313 AM EDT Monday...

1. Periods of rain Tuesday into Tuesday night before drying for 
Wednesday and Thursday.

2. A strong low pressure system passes through the St. Lawrence 
Valley and will bring widespread rainfall and breezy conditions 
Friday into Friday night, followed by a sharp cooldown.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 313 AM EDT Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: After a mostly dry but relatively dreary day today, the 
next round of rain will make its way into the region for tonight 
through tomorrow. A surface low will pass through from west to east, 
following a stationary boundary that will be in place ahead of time. 
While the low will be quick moving and technically more northern 
stream and not have a strong connection to Gulf/Atlantic moisture, 
it will include the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachael so there will 
be some efficient rainfall with the former tropical moisture. HREF 
probabilities of half an inch are between 70-100 percent for 
northern areas, dropping to between 50-70 for southern areas. 
Probabilities of an inch are between 50-80 percent for northern 
areas, dropping to the 10-40 percent range for southern areas. 
Overall, it will be a beneficial soaking rain. South of the front, 
meager instability will be able to develop. Combined with strong 
dynamics from the low, a couple stronger storms are possible, 
especially over southern St. Lawrence County. The exact northern 
extent will depend on the specific low track. Warm air aloft will 
remain on the backside so even though the cold front drops 
temperatures significantly, any upslope showers look to remain rain 
in the mountains. Conditions trend drier for Wednesday, but under a 
classic cyclonic northwest flow cold air advection regime, there 
will be some upslope sprinkles and showers but no widespread rain. 
Thursday looks dry, seasonably cool and should welcome the return of 
the sun for a bit.

KEY MESSAGE 2: An upper level trough and surface low pressure system 
will pass through the St Lawrence valley on Friday. Widespread rain 
is expected with this system as well as breezy conditions. 
Widespread rainfall amounts between 0.5 and one inch appear likely 
based on latest NWP consensus, and PoPs for late Friday are in the 
70-90% range. After the trailing cold front sweeps through, the 
temperatures will be much cooler through the weekend. The 12Z GFS 
depicts a particularly deep trough, consistent with previous runs. 
The 850mb temperatures on the GFS drop to -7C to -8C by 18Z 
Saturday, and then down to -8C to -9C by 18Z Sunday. While it is 
worth noting that the GFS tends to have a cold bias in these setups, 
the current forecast confidently reflects the potential for below-
normal temperatures based on the broader 12Z NWP model suite. Expect 
highs generally in the mid-upper 40s for both Saturday and Sunday, 
quite chilly. With a northwesterly flow and sufficient moisture in 
place, we cannot rule out upslope/mountain snow showers or flurries 
over the weekend, with some minor summit-level accumulations 
possible.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 12Z Tuesday...Widespread IFR and MVFR conditions this
morning with low ceilings and some BR. Rain has moved out of our
area. Conditions will be slow to recover this morning, and SLK
should remain IFR all day. Winds light and variable this morning
will shift to the NNW after 14z and remain less than 10 kts
through the period. More rain moves into our area from the north
overnight, and IFR conditions will be possible again overnight
with models indicating possible low stratus. 


Outlook...

Tuesday: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Definite SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Tuesday Night: Mainly IFR, with local MVFR possible. Definite
SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Wednesday: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Wednesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Thursday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Thursday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Friday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Definite SHRA.
